# The Portal's theme switch does nothing on its first click

**Claim it first:** comment on this issue before you start, and check the open pull requests for one that already points here. We merge the first approve-worthy PR (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`, point 3).

> **Corrected 2026-10-21:** the first version named only half of the trigger. The bug needs BOTH no stored `portalTheme` AND a light color-scheme preference. With a stored theme, or with dark mode, the first click works. Context, The Architectural Reality and the ACs now say so.

## Context

Welcome! This is a small fix in the Portal, the app behind neomjs.com (`apps/portal`). You need a fork, Node and the dev server; no Agent OS, Docker or AI tooling.

Found in release testing, 2026-10-20, with headless Chrome on a fresh profile. Headless Chrome reports `prefers-color-scheme: light`, and that is the second half of the trigger. The Portal loads in its dark theme, and the header's theme button shows a moon. The first click changes the icon but keeps the dark background. Only the second click switches to light.

Measured on neomjs.com, 2026-10-21, one fresh headless context per row:

| stored `portalTheme` | color scheme | first click |
|---|---|---|
| none | light | **stays dark**, icon moon → sun |
| none | dark | dark → light |
| `neo-theme-neo-dark` | light | dark → light |
| `neo-theme-neo-light` | light | light → dark |

**Who sees it:** a first-time visitor whose OS or browser is set to light, on their first click only. That click stores `portalTheme`, so every later visit works. Anyone who has clicked the button before, or uses dark mode, never sees it.

## The Problem

On that path, the first click asks for the theme that is already showing.

## The Architectural Reality

- `apps/portal/neo-config.json`: `"themes": ["neo-theme-neo-dark", …]`, so the Portal boots dark.
- `apps/portal/view/ViewportController.mjs#onConstructed` sets `viewport.theme` from a stored `portalTheme`, or to dark when `Neo.config.prefersDarkTheme` is true. With neither, it sets nothing.
- `#onSwitchTheme`: `oldTheme = viewport.theme || 'neo-theme-neo-light'`. On that third path `viewport.theme` is unset, so the method assumes light and "switches" to dark.
- `apps/portal/view/HeaderToolbar.mjs` starts the button with `iconCls: 'fa-solid fa-moon'`.
- Why: #8855 made dark the default by reordering `themes` in `neo-config.json`, a one-line change. The light fallback (from #8727) and the moon icon still assume the old light default.

## The Fix

When `viewport.theme` is unset, fall back to the theme the app actually booted with (the first entry of `themes`) instead of a hardcoded light. Make sure the button's starting icon matches that theme.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: with no stored `portalTheme` and a light color-scheme preference, one click on the theme button switches dark → light, and a second click switches back.
- [ ] AC-2: on that path, the button's icon matches the theme on screen before and after each click.

## Out of Scope

- Following the OS's light or dark preference. The dark default is deliberate.

## Related

- `apps/portal/view/ViewportController.mjs`, `apps/portal/view/HeaderToolbar.mjs`.

### @abhinav-rb - 2026-10-21T00:06:47Z

Hi! I'd like to take this one. Could I be assigned?

Plan:
- In `ViewportController#onSwitchTheme`, read the current theme with `viewport.getTheme()` instead of `viewport.theme || 'neo-theme-neo-light'`. `getTheme()` already falls back to `themes[0]`, so the first click on a fresh load goes from dark to light (AC-1).
- Pull the icon logic out of `setTheme()` into a small `updateThemeSwitchIcon()` helper and call it from `onConstructed` when there's no stored theme and no dark preference. That way the button shows the sun on a dark boot instead of the static moon (AC-2).
- Add cases to `ViewportController.spec.mjs` for a fresh dark boot, a fresh light boot, and the icon mapping.
